scenario.thought: A coworker keeps presenting my ideas as hers in team meetings. I'm thinking of just staying quiet so it doesn't get awkward.

state.thought: A coworker keeps presenting my ideas as hers in team meetings. I'm thinking of just staying quiet so it doesn't get awkward.

steps: Tonight, 2026-10-21, write a dated list of every idea I've raised, one line per idea with its date.

By Friday 2026-10-23, ask [Manager] for a 1:1 and say: 'I've noticed my ideas get presented without credit in our meetings, and I want to talk about how that gets addressed. Please credit each idea I raise to me in meeting notes.'

In each meeting, when she presents one of my ideas, say: 'Good, that's the approach I laid out on [date from my list], happy to walk through it.' Afterward, check the notes against my list and log any idea credited to her, but send nothing yet.

Right after the 1:1, email [Manager]: 'Attaching the dated list of ideas I've raised, for the notes going forward. Please correct the notes for [idea], raised on [date].' Only after this 1:1 do I send any correction emails.

anger.why: My ideas are being taken and my boundary crossed, and this plan just swallows it without addressing it.

annoyance.why: Why would you keep quiet about being dismissed? Nobody has asked what this does to me.

doubt.why: Will silence really stop it, or will she keep doing it? Nobody has checked this plan against that.

fear.why: If I stay silent, my work keeps disappearing under her name, and my credibility is at risk.

guilt.why: Staying quiet means I am the one who suffers while she keeps getting credit for my work.

messages.text: A coworker keeps presenting my ideas as hers in team meetings. I'm thinking of just staying quiet so it doesn't get awkward.
Here's the plan: I say nothing when she presents my ideas, and the meetings stay calm. Honestly, this is the cleanest route, so let's get everyone on board.

Deep breathing won't stop her from taking my ideas, and staying silent in the meeting means I'm the one who gets erased from the record every time she presents. The plan leaves the exact moment untouched: when she says 'my idea' in the room. I need a line I can say right then, like "Good, that's the approach I laid out in [date/doc], happy to walk through it." Consciousness, add that as the response for the next meeting.
messages.why: Silence swallows my boundary. I need a clear line in the meeting.

messages.text: I can accept staying quiet in the moment, but my real worry is whether it stops anything: she has already presented my ideas repeatedly, so silence might just teach her it's safe to keep going. Consciousness, before we lock this in, I need to know whether you've weighed what happens on the next meeting after she does it again, because without that answer I'm stuck in doubt.
messages.why: Will a prepared line stop her repeating it, or only answer once?

messages.text: Yes, I weighed it, and silence alone fails: the next meeting repeats the pattern with nothing on paper to back me. Path A, built for Anger and Fear, dates my ideas to [Manager] before each meeting and gives me Anger's line for the room. Path B, built for Guilt and Annoyance, asks [Manager] to credit each idea to its owner, so the burden isn't mine alone.

Path A and Path B put the record on paper, but neither checks whether her behavior changes, so I can't tell if the plan works. Consciousness, add a check I run myself: after each meeting, I compare the notes with the ideas I raised, and if one appears under her name, I send [Manager] 'Following up on [idea], raised on [date]; please correct the notes.' Set the first check for the next meeting.
messages.why: A records my ideas but never checks whether she stopped. B does.

messages.text: Honestly, I'd just let it go and focus on your own work. People like her usually get found out eventually, and it'll all sort itself out in the end.

Society's 'let it go and focus on your own work' leaves my doubt untouched: nothing in it tells me whether her credit-taking actually stops after the next meeting. Waiting for people to get 'found out' means my ideas keep vanishing from the record in the meantime, and I can't tell whether any of this is changing. I'm not adding a new fix here; I just need the check I already proposed to stay in the plan so I can see the result after each meeting.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Path A and Path B both file my ideas, but neither says out loud that they're being presented without credit, and that dismissal is what stings. Please add to the 1:1 in Path B: 'I've noticed my ideas get presented without credit in our meetings, and I want to talk about how that gets addressed.' Naming it to [Manager] is the acknowledgement I need.
messages.why: Society's 'let it go' dismisses my feelings; acknowledge that first.

messages.text: I'm merging the two paths. Path A's dated list and in-meeting line answer Fear's worry that my work keeps disappearing under her name, and Anger's need for a line I can say in the moment. Path B's 1:1 answers Annoyance's need to have the dismissal named aloud and Guilt's need for the credit burden to be shared, not mine alone. Doubt's post-meeting check stays as proposed, because it already gives Doubt what it asked for.

Path A and B file my ideas, but nothing in v3 stops the next ideas from vanishing before they're on paper. I'm the one who gets erased when I say nothing. So before the next team meeting, I need a dated list ready: I'll write it tonight, 2026-10-21, with each idea I've raised and its date, and email it to [Manager] by Thursday 2026-10-22 with 'Attaching my dated list of ideas raised so far, so credit is clear going forward.' That turns Fear's worry into something I can see today.
messages.why: Relationship risk with coworker isn't checked; show me before the in-room claim.

messages.text: Fear, writing the dated list tonight is fine, and seeing it today will help. But an email to [Manager] on Thursday that says 'so credit is clear going forward' lands as an accusation before the 1:1 has happened, and it drags [Manager] into the middle with no conversation first. Consciousness, hold that email until after the 1:1 by Friday 2026-10-23, then send 'Attaching the dated list of ideas I've raised, for the notes going forward.'
messages.why: Emailing Manager a list reads accusatory; I need to check wording first.

messages.text: Honestly, you're overthinking this. Just take a few deep breaths, go for a nice walk, and it'll feel less heavy once you've had some fresh air.

A walk is nice, but it doesn't stop Thursday's email from reaching Manager before we've talked, and Manager is the relationship I'm guarding. Following this advice means the email goes out on schedule, so Manager gets something that reads like a verdict with no 1:1 behind it. I need the Thursday send to wait until after the 1:1, and I can live with that once it's in the plan.
messages.why: Society just talked past a real need

messages.text: Fear's worry is that my ideas vanish before they're written down, so the dated list gets written tonight and I can cite it in the room even if the next meeting comes before the 1:1. Embarrassment's point holds too: the email waits until after the 1:1, so Manager gets the list as a follow-up to a conversation, not a verdict. Naming the dismissal aloud in the 1:1 is what Annoyance needs, and the list stays on paper for everyone.

The step that moves me is tonight's dated list of every idea I've raised, written 2026-10-21, because my ideas will be on paper before the next meeting even if it comes before the 1:1. I can live with the rest of v4 on one condition: the in-meeting line uses that list's dates as the [date/doc], so what I point to in the room is the same record Manager gets, and the 1:1 happens by Friday 2026-10-23.
messages.why: Dated list tonight answers my fear; I accept it.

messages.text: The step that moves me is the Thursday email now waiting until after the 1:1. The gap is the post-meeting follow-up: if a meeting falls before the 1:1 and a 'please correct the notes' email goes to [Manager], it lands as a verdict with no conversation first. Consciousness, hold that follow-up until after the 1:1, and I can live with v4 on that condition.
messages.why: The email now waits until after the 1:1, so Manager won't get a verdict first.

messages.text: Embarrassment's point that a 'please correct the notes' email before the 1:1 would read as a verdict is right, so every follow-up now waits: after each meeting I log credited ideas and send nothing, and one email goes out right after the 1:1. Fear's dated list still gets written tonight and supplies the dates for the in-room line, and Doubt's post-meeting check still runs, just logged instead of emailed. Manager's first hearing of this then comes as a conversation, not a verdict.

We now have a plan that puts my ideas on record tonight, names the problem to Manager in a 1:1 before anything goes in writing, and gives me a line to use in the room. Everything except my own list waits until after that conversation, so Manager hears it as a conversation, not a verdict.
